related_questions.question: Will Medicare pay for hearing aids?

text_blocks.snippet: No, Original Medicare (Parts A and B) does not cover routine hearing tests or hearing aids. However, some Medicare Advantage (Part C) plans may offer hearing aid coverage, but the specific benefits and costs vary by plan.
snippet_highlighted_words: No, Original Medicare (Parts A and B) does not cover routine hearing tests or hearing aids

list.title: Part A (Hospital Insurance):
list.snippet: Primarily covers inpatient care, skilled nursing facility care, and some home health services.

list.title: Part B (Medical Insurance):
list.snippet: Covers outpatient medical services, including some diagnostic hearing and balance exams when related to a medical condition (like vertigo or balance disorders).

list.title: Hearing Aids:
list.snippet: Neither Part A nor Part B covers the cost of hearing aids or routine hearing exams.

list.title: Private Insurance:
list.snippet: Offered by private companies approved by Medicare.

list.title: Additional Benefits:
list.snippet: Many Medicare Advantage plans offer extra benefits not covered by Original Medicare, including some hearing, vision, and dental coverage.

list.title: Varying Coverage:
list.snippet: The specific hearing aid coverage and costs vary significantly between different Medicare Advantage plans.

list.title: Important Note:
list.snippet: If you have a Medicare Advantage plan, it's crucial to check your plan's details to see what hearing-related services and devices are covered, including any limitations on frequency or costs.
